# A02 — Copula / Self-Identity through Difference

<!-- paired-field-navigation -->
[Argument field](README.md) · [Other face: A02′ — Continuity as Maintained Identification](conjugate/A02-prime-Continuity-as-Maintained-Identification.md) · [Shared A/C root](conjugate/AC.md)
<!-- /paired-field-navigation -->

## #0 — Identity has a passage to make

An identity must be recognised, stated, remembered or carried across a difference of presentation. Even “A is A” makes a minimal journey: the second inscription is not the first inscription, yet the judgment identifies them. The copula keeps them together through the difference that gives the act of identification its work.

**Identity is maintained through difference, rather than achieved by erasing it.** The copula identifies what it distinguishes and distinguishes what it identifies in one act. The [copular operation](concepts/C06-Copula-Identification-with-Difference.md) also gives [faithful definition](A01-Subject-God-and-Faithful-Definition.md) its obligation: identification can be exact without enclosing the condition of the identifying act.

Opposition requires a shared register in which the opposed terms can meet. Assertion and denial must be distinguishable within the field where they address one another. What is being held the same, what differs, and through which relation can the two answer to one another? The common relation gives each distinction its place and makes its consequences examinable.

For self-knowledge, both sides of that question matter. A self must differ from itself in presentation to have something to recognise, and remain itself for the recognition to be self-knowledge. At the [subjective pole](concepts/C01-Subject-Defined-Indefinability.md), the present act cannot be reduced to a finished self-image. Yet the changing image need not sever the identity it articulates. The copula is the capacity to cross this difference while keeping the seam available.

## #1 — This very one through altered predicates

The copula has a double office. **Predication** attaches content: this is red, tired, remembered, expected. **Identification** holds the instance to which the content belongs: this is that very one. When a description changes, identification keeps the change attributable. When identification is asserted, a determinate presentation makes the assertion available. One act carries these two distinguishable moments.

Consider two people with the same name. Repeating the name does not decide which person is meant. Conversely, a change of name does not, by itself, make its bearer another person. Naming therefore presupposes an individuation it cannot accomplish by the sound of the name alone. Beneath the name, counting holds the unique instance being named. “Counting” here means distinguishing this occurrence from another, before an explicit numeral or a public name has been assigned.

That priority is an order of constitution. A name becomes effective through a distinguished instance, and its effective use can subsequently reshape how distinctions are made. The pre-nominal counter is the office of “this very one” within the continuing act of identification.

The difference between “is” and “equals” gives the office a second face. An equation identifies expressions whose forms differ. In the elementary equality below, the right side articulates what the left gathers:

$$
3 = 1 + 2.
$$

The expressions are unequal as inscriptions and equal in the respect the equation states. Their equality does not abolish the difference through which it can be recognised. Predicative content and numerical identification remain distinct operations even where ordinary speech lets one word carry both. [Determination](concepts/C03-Determination.md) gives each assertion its scope by discriminating the respect in which it applies.

## #2 — Circumstance makes the identification answerable

To identify this as that very one also requires **circumstance**. A name can be shared; a description can be repeated; an image can be copied. The field of comparison determines which sameness is at issue. The person standing here, the person recalled yesterday, the figure in a photograph and a fictional character bearing the same name do not become interchangeable because one string can designate them.

Identification therefore joins three moments: **name, instance and circumstance**. The name makes a determination articulable; the instance holds what is being identified; the circumstance supplies the horizon in which the identification and its alternatives can be compared. Identity is name and instance proposed relative to circumstance. “Proposed” does not mean arbitrary. It means that a claim of identity has a place, a criterion and consequences for which it can answer.

Context can disambiguate a scope that a bare formula has not settled. The question is not only which words occur but what this use of them expresses, who is speaking, and which possibility is being entertained. The circumstantial whole supplies an ordering within which particular distinctions are made. Someone can identify a remembered person, distinguish a fictional namesake and entertain an alternative history because the act holds the respect under which each is being compared.

[Encounter becomes accountable identification](../../symbolon/episteme/etymologies/encounter-region-name-count/WHOLE-FIELD-encounter-region-name-count.md) by keeping address active within counting. A person can count as one participant without becoming exhausted by the count. [Constitutive exclusion](A08-Apoha-Constitutive-Exclusion.md) gives naming its differential reach: deciding which instance counts also excludes alternatives, and those exclusions remain conditions of the decision.

For example, the thirty-six stipulated outcomes of two dice vary the state while retaining which dice are being varied. The counterfactual situation is intelligible through the identity and conditions held in the comparison. The number of possibilities belongs to this specified experiment; the example shows how alternatives can be compared without losing their referents.

[Language in practice](../../symbolon/episteme/histories/traditions-and-disciplines/language-symbol-dialogue/DEVELOPMENT-language-symbol-dialogue.md#language-practice) gives this circumstantial account its social extension: speakers maintain and alter identifications through how they use them together.

Succession adds another pressure. “One more” requires retaining what has already been counted while distinguishing a further occurrence. The counted unit must be alike enough to join the count and different enough to increase it. Running this operation gives counting its temporal articulation: the prior occurrence is held while the next is admitted. Memory and comparison belong to the act of counting itself: what has been counted remains available while the count changes.

## #3 — The relation includes its own operation

The copula now returns upon its own identifying activity. The account has distinguished names, instances and circumstances; it must also account for the act that drew those distinctions. If circumstance is represented as another item, the present act of representing that item still occurs within a circumstance. Its representation can deepen the account without enclosing the condition of the act now making it. This [non-coincidence](A03-Immutable-Gap-Formal-Limit.md) recurs within representation itself: the [formal limit](concepts/C04-Formal-Limit.md) is generated by the attempt to enclose the act in its own account.

Two propositions remain together: distinctions are really makeable, and nothing determined is wholly detached from the field in which its distinction is made. The first permits exact identification. The second makes that identification answerable. The copula collapses when “same” becomes “indistinguishable”; it breaks when “different” becomes “unrelated.” Keeping its two offices active permits a determination to return as the same through alteration.

The [copular construction](../../symbolon/matheme/definition/copula.md) makes the two offices inspectable. Two parallel strokes can be recognised as the same kind of stroke because their placement distinguishes them. Equality therefore works through a difference; difference becomes intelligible through a relation held equal. The bond `=` and the cut `/` compose the unequal sign `≠`. The full expression holds identity, identity-in-relation-to-difference, difference-in-relation-to-identity and difference within one relating act:

$$
/ = (= =/≠ ≠).
$$

The slash permits the faces to be distinguished **OR** held together **AND**. Identity articulated through difference and identity distinguished from difference are different respects of one identification. Keeping both lets a relation be exact without making its presentations indistinguishable. The four appearances are composed through two operations, cut and bond: `4+2`. When the middle is held as one hinge rather than opened into its two faces, the same account becomes three terms within one field, `(3+1)+2`. The [harmonic recount](../../symbolon/matheme/definition/harmonics-and-recount.md) changes the level of accounting while preserving what the first count distinguished.

The [eight determinations](../../symbolon/eight-determinations.md) carry this operation beyond the graphic construction. At `X/x`, determining capacity and indefinite particular become readable through one letter in different cases. At `AM/IS`, that relation becomes personed: what can be said of a life belongs within the lived context in which “I,” “you” and “it” have their places. The act can then receive a determinate expression without exhausting the capacity to differentiate further, the passage into `∞/dx`.

The unity of the relation can be [singular One or polyvalent All](A11-The-Two-Ones-0-One-1-All.md). As [Mono/Poly](A12-Mono-Poly-One-All-Whole-Many.md), one whole holds many determinations without erasing their differences. As [dia/syn](A13-Two-Logics-of-Two-Dia-Syn.md), differentiation and return give conjugate accountings of those determinations. Each makes a different consequence of identification operative: unity, multiplicity and the manner of their relating.

## #4 — Persons become available within one context

“I,” “you” and “it” make circumstance felt from within speech. “I” changes its bearer as speakers change, while retaining its first-person office in the utterance. “You” addresses another whose reply can change what the speaker means. “It” makes something available for shared predication. Address participates in how the persons and their object become available to one another.

The position-sensitive use of “I” differs from attaching a given name to its bearer. The same utterance can be mine as speaker, yours as addressee, and an object of description. Their relation makes the speech event shareable while preserving the different places from which it is lived.

The `1–2–3` pass follows the persons in sequence. The `4–5–0` recognition pass voids their isolation, recognises their unity and returns the achieved account to the relation through which it arose. Context does not insert a fourth pronoun. It makes the three positions available together, including the activity by which they were distinguished. Their unity does not erase the first-person, second-person and third-person differences. This is why the two triads can be read as `3:3` and as `3:1`: the recognition pass gathers the preceding three as one act. Its operation is different from the `4:2` distinction between four explicate positions and two implicate poles.

The fourth still permits an account *about* this unity. [Faithful definition](A01-Subject-God-and-Faithful-Definition.md) requires a further turn: an explanation that all the persons belong to one activity has not yet performed its first-person recognition. A richer description of the speaker is still a description. The copula must return in the mode of the one for whom the identification matters.

[Lived first-person appearing, organising identity, self-image and whole-Self](concepts/C35-Selfing-Self-Subjectivity-Self-Thing.md) have distinct offices within this recognition. The crucial consequence is interpersonal: representing a self does not acquire the first-person presence whose life the representation concerns. A model of another can become more exact and still remain a model within an encounter. [The other's capacity to answer](A27-Self-and-Other-Unity-without-Possession.md) makes the identification responsive to someone whom it does not possess.

## #5→0 — The identifying act recognises itself

**The identification must be mine.** The personal circuit makes the turn explicit:

$$
\text{I = Is}
\;\rightarrow\;
\text{Who I am = What is}
\;\rightarrow\;
\text{What I am = Who is?}
\;\rightarrow\;
\text{I = Am}.
$$

The first “is” makes being available as a statement. “Who I am = What is” places my identity in relation to what can be said to be. The next turn changes the office of “what I am”: **the equating itself is what I am**, and its differential is “who is?” The one making the identification can no longer remain a spectator outside the relation being identified. The question returns the completed account to its own act. “Am” is that identification spoken from within.

This is why the last turn changes the first. The speaker has passed through determinate descriptions and their relation, and recognises the activity by which they belonged to one account. The subject's definition directs attention to this act of self-designation. As the identification is made, its limit-name relinquishes the demand for another predicate that would finally contain the one who predicates. The [faithful definition of the subject](A01-Subject-God-and-Faithful-Definition.md) is fulfilled through the performance of the relation it defines.

In [recognition](concepts/C19-Pratyabhijna-Recognition.md), the return occurs through changed form: the change has become part of what is recognised. [Individuation](A21-Individuation-Recognition.md) carries this relation through the longer movement of a life. A name can remain answerable through altered descriptions because identity is sustained in relation, and the relation can itself become more explicit. The return preserves what the passage has differentiated.

The account also returns to its own accountability. What it counts, the marks it attaches, and the circumstance that lets those marks matter become available for renewed judgment. [Cross-register sameness](../../symbolon/episteme/etymologies/homology-and-analogy/WHOLE-FIELD-homology-and-analogy.md) depends on the operation and respect of comparison. [Focal return and qualified predication](concepts/C63-Pros-Hen-In-Quantum-Focal-Return-Qualified-Predication.md) keep that respect explicit; an [order of dependence](A34-Idealism-Order-of-Dependence.md) can hold where the kinds of sameness and priority differ between registers. The comparison remains exact by stating which relation holds and in what respect it holds.

The copula returns as the relation already enacted in the first assertion: exact enough to identify, open enough for the identified to answer through difference.

In [The Prisoner](../../symbolon/mytheme/worlds/british-television/the-prisoner/WHOLE.md#prisoner-asymmetric-count), the Village’s designation identifies a position within its field, while Number Six’s reply refuses to let that predicate exhaust the speaker. Assigned identity and first-person address meet through this difference: designation and refusal belong to one encounter without becoming equivalent accounts of it.
